title: AI Moves Into The Workday
pattern: The signal is no longer that AI might someday change work. The signal is that companies are already using it to redraw roles, expectations, and leverage. The human task is to stop treating identity as a job title and start naming the value that travels with you.

stories.title: AI skills are becoming part of the hiring baseline at the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency
stories.summary: This matters to The Great Repurpose because it separates the human being from the job wrapper around them. AI literacy is becoming part of the baseline expectation for knowledge work, which means people need to name the human value that travels with them as the role keeps changing.
keyPoints: The intelligence agency is reshaping training for both new and existing employees as it builds AI and data management into core job expectations across the workforce.
AI fluency is moving from specialist skill to everyday job requirement.
The TGR signal is that workers need a durable sense of value beyond any single job description.

stories.title: Adobe’s AI Edge: Turning Solo Creators Into Global Media Brands
stories.summary: This matters because it points to the human value that remains when execution gets automated. AI may multiply output, but the creator's taste, judgment, point of view, and relationship with an audience become the real scarce assets.
keyPoints: Adobe research says 87% of creators report AI is accelerating growth while making creativity and judgment more valuable.
Solo creators can now operate with leverage once reserved for larger media teams.
The TGR signal is that human voice and direction matter more as production gets easier.

stories.title: AI is redefining entry-level roles – and young workers have the edge
stories.summary: This matters to The Great Repurpose because it separates the human being from the job wrapper around them. Entry-level work is being renegotiated first, so young workers need more than tool familiarity; they need a clearer sense of purpose and value as the first rung changes shape.
keyPoints: Recruitment experts say AI literacy is now a baseline expectation for graduates entering the workforce.
The early-career bargain is changing as AI absorbs parts of the work people used to learn on.
The TGR signal is that the first job matters less as an identity anchor and more as a launchpad for direction.

stories.title: Tech Layoffs Hit 1,115 a Day in 2026: Companies Cite AI but Cuts Fail to Boost Returns
stories.summary: This matters to The Great Repurpose because it separates the human being from the job wrapper around them. Companies are citing AI as a reason to cut roles, but the deeper story is that identity and security cannot be outsourced to an employer's latest operating model.
keyPoints: Tech layoffs in 2026 are averaging 1,115 job cuts per day as companies cite artificial intelligence to justify eliminating roles.
A Gartner study cited in the story found companies cutting the most showed no improvement in financial returns.
The TGR signal is that AI is becoming a management narrative as much as a technology story.

stories.title: AI Made Content Abundant. For Creators, Voice Is Now The Scarce Asset
stories.summary: This matters because it points to the human value that remains when execution gets automated. As AI floods the world with competent content, the differentiator becomes the perspective people trust and recognize as genuinely human.
keyPoints: A 2026 survey of 16,000 creators shows voice and judgment, not volume, are now the scarce asset.
AI makes publishing easier, but it also makes generic output less valuable.
The TGR signal is that creators need to reclaim voice as durable human value and use AI to amplify it.
